topics.topic: Mission 100% Electrification: Powering the Future of Indian Railways
topics.why_in_news: Indian Railways achieved around 99.2% Broad Gauge electrification under Mission 100% Electrification, marking a major milestone in sustainable transport and infrastructure modernisation.
prelims_quick_notes: Railway electrification replaces diesel traction with electric traction.
Electric traction improves energy efficiency and reduces fuel dependence.
Mission aims for complete Broad Gauge electrification.
Indian Railways among world’s largest electrified rail networks.
Solar power integration increasing across railway infrastructure.
Electrification supports low-carbon transport transition.
Electric locomotives have lower operational and maintenance costs.
Rail infrastructure modernisation linked with logistics competitiveness.
important_facts: Indian Railways achieved about 99.2% BG electrification by November 2025.
Broad Gauge is dominant railway gauge in India.
Overhead Equipment (OHE) used for electric traction supply.
Solar capacity on railway network expanded significantly after 2014.
Switzerland has nearly 100% rail electrification.
Electric traction more energy efficient than diesel traction.
key_highlights: Electrification pace accelerated sharply after 2014.
Large-scale solar integration implemented.
Automatic Wiring Train used for faster OHE installation.
Mechanised construction improved execution efficiency.
Reduced diesel dependence and emissions highlighted.
exam_relevance: Important for Economy, Infrastructure and Energy Security.
Useful for sustainable transport and logistics topics.
Can be linked with climate goals and green infrastructure.
prelims_traps: Electrification relates mainly to Broad Gauge network.
OHE used in electric railway traction systems.
Solar power integrated for traction and non-traction uses.
Electric traction reduces dependence on imported diesel.

topics.why_in_news: India’s fisheries and aquaculture sector recorded major growth in production, exports and employment generation, supported by policy reforms and Blue Economy initiatives.
prelims_quick_notes: Fisheries among fastest-growing agri-allied sectors in India.
Sector includes capture fisheries and aquaculture.
Blue Economy promotes sustainable use of marine resources.
India is among largest fish producers globally.
Aquaculture increasingly important for exports and livelihoods.
Fisheries contribute significantly to agricultural GVA.
Digital platforms and traceability systems expanding in sector.
Sustainable fishing and deep-sea resource management emphasised.
important_facts: PMMSY launched in 2020.
Department of Fisheries functions under Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
India ranks second globally in fish production.
India ranks first in shrimp exports.
EEZ stands for Exclusive Economic Zone.
Seaweed farming promoted as sustainable aquaculture practice.
Fisheries largely State subject while EEZ under Union domain.
ONDC integration expanded for fisheries FFPOs.
key_highlights: Fish production more than doubled since 2013–14.
Exports crossed ₹62,000 crore in FY 2024–25.
Employment generation increased significantly.
National Fisheries Digital Platform promoted formalisation.
Cluster-based fisheries development expanded.
Biofloc, cage culture and seaweed farming encouraged.
exam_relevance: Important for Economy, Blue Economy and Rural Livelihoods.
Useful for coastal development and sustainable resource management topics.
Can be linked with exports, food security and climate resilience.
prelims_traps: India ranks second in fish production globally.
Seaweed farming considered low-impact and sustainable aquaculture.

topics.why_in_news: NITI Aayog released Export Preparedness Index (EPI) 2024 assessing export readiness and competitiveness of States and Union Territories.
prelims_quick_notes: EPI measures export preparedness of States and UTs.
Prepared by NITI Aayog.
Focus on sub-national export competitiveness.
Supports district-based export planning strategy.
Encourages cooperative and competitive federalism.
Index evaluates infrastructure, governance and business ecosystem.
MSME ecosystem important component in export competitiveness.
Aligns with Districts as Export Hubs initiative.
important_facts: First EPI released in 2020.
EPI 2024 has 4 pillars, 13 sub-pillars and 70 indicators.
Business Ecosystem carries highest weightage at 40%.
Large States category topped by Maharashtra.
EPI focuses on preparedness, not export volume alone.
Index supports place-based export development strategies.
key_highlights: Greater emphasis on MSME ecosystem and cost competitiveness.
District-level export planning strengthened.
Human capital and logistics included in framework.
Policy benchmarking among states encouraged.
Digital trade facilitation and GVC integration emphasised.
exam_relevance: Important for Economy, Exports and Federal Governance.
Useful for logistics, MSMEs and global trade topics.
Can be linked with competitive federalism and industrial policy.
prelims_traps: EPI measures preparedness, not export performance alone.
Business Ecosystem pillar has highest weightage.
District export planning linked with DEH initiative.

topics.why_in_news: Economic Survey 2025–26 highlighted India’s resilient macroeconomic fundamentals, robust growth outlook, low inflation and strengthening fiscal and financial indicators.
prelims_quick_notes: Economic Survey tabled before Union Budget every year.
Prepared under guidance of Chief Economic Adviser.
Survey analyses macroeconomic trends and policy priorities.
India projected to maintain strong medium-term growth.
Services sector remains major contributor to GDP.
Inflation moderated significantly during FY26.
Capital expenditure continues as major growth driver.
Financial inclusion and banking-sector health improved.
important_facts: Economic Survey is non-statutory document.
Real GDP growth projected around 6.8–7.2% for FY27.
Services contribute largest share to India’s GDP.
Foreign exchange reserves crossed USD 700 billion.
PLI schemes expanded manufacturing investment and jobs.
RBI Financial Inclusion Index improved further in 2025.
Gross NPAs declined to multi-decadal lows.
India became seventh-largest services exporter globally.
key_highlights: Historic decline in CPI inflation recorded.
Manufacturing and services sectors showed strong momentum.
Banking-sector indicators improved significantly.
Capital expenditure and fiscal credibility strengthened.
Exports and remittance inflows remained resilient.
Female LFPR and labour participation improved.
exam_relevance: Important for Economy, Fiscal Policy and Macroeconomic Indicators.
Useful for inflation, banking and growth topics.
Can be linked with employment, exports and financial inclusion.
prelims_traps: Economic Survey is not a constitutional document.
Prepared before presentation of Union Budget.
Real GDP differs from nominal GDP.
Foreign exchange reserves strengthen external-sector resilience.
